✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Compact and cute clash. With only few hours left, I realised this was a contribution I'd be glad to see implemented.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: cool, simple and entertaining CoC
I think this clash is inadequate for reverse mode; the rules are easy to understand, but too much specific to just guess. This is only my opinion, I'm gladly accepting any counterargument.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Nice execution! Clear and rather subtle rules. Works for all modes.

Definitely approved! :)
Why is Test 4's answer 2 instead of 3?
There are some typos and formatting issues, and the stub generator lacks a write statement. Please fix those first. Thanks.
I think it's done, have you got any remarks to do, i've maybe forgotten some errors, but I don't see them.

because the alarm of the second door is "on".
When an alarm is "on", you can pass the door's alarm, but you can't continue the game. y'oure arrested by the alarm, even if the next door is open.

The rules arn't to hard to understand when we only have the tests and the results.
I understand your point of view, but if a player look at the title in reverse mode, he can easily understand the princip and I can maybe add the word "alarm" in the title to help them.

codingamers will maybe had difficulties with the rule when the alarm is on, but it's not too hard to understand after few tests
The title of the clash isn't shown during a clash in Reverse mode.
ha, ok, so should I remove the reverse mode ?

Well, the current tests don't provide enough guidance. Based on the first four visible tests alone, I could conclude that the task is simply to count the number of occurrences of "unlocked off", only to get stuck on Test 5.

Unless more representative visible tests are added, I think it's better to disable Reverse mode.

Ok, it's done
Thanks for your detailled and explained point of view

I see, so the logic here is:

unlocked, off: pass through the door, continue with the next door
unlocked, on: pass through the door, unable to continue
locked, off: do not pass through the door, continue with the next door
locked, on: do not pass through the door, unable to continue

Is this the intended reasoning?

Not exactly, 
the two first lines ar right.
but when a door is locked, you can't pass, even if the alarm is off. You're stopped by the locked doors in your count.
You must see the string like a corridor.

I see, thanks for clarifying. Perhaps it would be helpful to mention this concept of the input sequence being like a long corridor in the problem description? Maybe something like:

"There is a house made up of a long corridor of [[nd]] doors. You want to pass through as many doors in the corridor (from left to right) as you can to reach the furthest point in the house. However, the house has an alarm system."

Ok, thank you very much, it's a good modification.

I hope, you'll upvote or approved my contribution.
Try taking a look at the formatting in the Input section and running the Constraints section through a spell checker.

Shame on me for my bad english.
Thanks for indicating me where to take a look for correcting myself the errors of language.

Have you got any other remark to do ?

Do remember to run the spell checker and double-check the statement before making the contribution public 😉

Constraints
* Please change "before the next door, while that one is unlocked" to "and cannot go through the next door".

* Just to clarify: are we supposed to be able to go through an unlocked door even if its alarm is on?

* Please move the final three lines to the Goal section.

Goal
* Please change "have enter" to "want to enter".

Input
* Please add:
The doors are given in the order in which you encounter them.

Output
* Please change "have passed" to "can pass".

Cases
* Test 5: Please change the last "locked off" to "unlocked off" to match Validator 5.

* Validator 5:
  • Please remove the trailing newline from the input.
  • Please change "unlocked on" to "locked on" to match Test 5.

Thanks.

Thanks you so much.
I'll remember to check the spell of each sentence before making it public.

No worries.

Goal
* Please change "(mainwhile" to "even if", and change ")" to ".".

Output
* The second sentence should appear in Input, not Output.

Thanks.
It's done
